newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Brash declines comment on market's easing.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Brash declines comment on market's easing.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) Governor Don Brash on Friday declined to comment on the sharp market-led easing in New Zealand monetary conditions that has followed comments he made to a wire agency on Thursday.
Asked by Reuters how appropriate he judged the market-led change in conditions to have been, he replied, via a spokesman, "No comment".
Asked whether he had any intention to communicate his view of current monetary conditions to a wider audience via a press statement, he also said "no comment".

Since Brash's comments were reported on Thursday afternoon 90-day bank bill rates have dropped 20 basis points to 6.83 percent from 7.03 percent, and the dollar has weakened on its Trade-Weighted Index to 68.45 from 68.90.
Wholesale rates had already been falling steadily in recent weeks as economic data has indicated more benign inflation prospects than many market observers had been expecting.
The next formal statement on monetary policy is expected in the RBNZ's six-monthly update due in June.
